about.title: Passionate about transforming
about.para1: I work at CDI Portugal, where I develop and coordinate educational projects in programming, robotics and digital literacy at the Digital Citizenship Centre of Valongo and the Carlos Fiolhais Innovation Centre in Maia.
about.para2: I specialise in the pedagogical design of STEAM activities, technology clubs and projects with a strong hands-on component — educational robotics, artificial intelligence, gamification and digital citizenship.

stats.quote: "Education should be practical, meaningful and connected to the real world."

methodology.title: How I work
methodology.subtitle: Every learning experience I design follows solid pedagogical principles, adapted to the context and audience.

methods.title: Active Learning
methods.description: I place the learner at the centre of the experience. Instead of transmitting knowledge, I create situations where it is built through action, exploration and reflection.

methods.title: Computational Thinking
methods.description: I teach learners to decompose problems, identify patterns and create systematic solutions — a skill that goes far beyond programming.

methods.title: STEAM Methodologies
methods.description: I integrate Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Maths in interdisciplinary projects that connect knowledge and develop creative thinking.

methods.title: Practical Projects (PBL)
methods.description: Every project has a real product, a real audience and a real presentation. Learning becomes meaningful when the outcome is concrete and shareable.

gameDesign.title: Game elements in learning
gameDesign.subtitle: I incorporate game design mechanics to create more engaging, motivating and effective learning experiences.

elements.title: Missions
elements.description: Clear, challenging objectives that keep learners focused. Each mission is calibrated to be stimulating without being frustrating.

elements.title: Levels & Progression
elements.description: Progressive scaffolding that ensures no one falls behind or gets bored. Each level builds on the previous one.

elements.title: Immediate Feedback
elements.description: Mistakes aren't failures — they're learning. Fast, constructive feedback transforms every attempt into a growth opportunity.

elements.title: Achievements
elements.description: Visible milestones and celebration of progress. Making growth tangible is highly motivating for any learner.

elements.title: Narrative
elements.description: A good story gives context and meaning. I transform exercises into challenges and classrooms into worlds to explore.

gameDesign.theoryTitle: The books that ground my practice
gameDesign.theorySubtitle: My approach to educational game design is supported by recognised academic research and professional practice.

books.author: Karl M. Kapp
books.title: The Gamification of Learning and Instruction
books.idea: Game-based thinking and mechanics can be applied directly to instructional design to create intrinsically motivating learning experiences.
books.application: I use missions, point systems, level progression and positive reinforcement to transform dry content into experiences where learners want to keep going. The key is calibrated challenge — not too easy, not too hard.

books.author: Karl M. Kapp
books.title: The Gamification of Learning and Instruction Fieldbook
books.idea: A practical implementation guide: how to transform learning objectives into functional game structures within real educational contexts.
books.application: This book gives me the operational framework: how to map competencies to missions, how to build pedagogical narratives and how to use feedback loops to keep learners in a state of flow throughout the entire experience.

books.author: Jesse Schell
books.title: The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses
books.idea: 113 lenses — unique perspectives — for analysing and improving any game experience, always placing the player at the centre of design.
books.application: I apply Schell's lenses to learning design: the Lens of Experience (what does the learner feel?), the Lens of Challenge (is it calibrated?), and the Lens of Curiosity (what makes them want to know more?). Learner-centred design starts with these questions.

books.author: Steven L. Kent
books.title: The Ultimate History of Video Games
books.idea: How video games evolved from a niche curiosity to a global cultural phenomenon — and what that tells us about what makes an experience irresistibly engaging.
books.application: Understanding the history of games helps me identify universal psychological principles of engagement: visible progression, autonomy, identity and community. These are the same principles I apply to create learning experiences that learners simply don't want to leave.

motivations.title: Why I do this
motivations.quote: "I believe teaching technology is teaching how to think. And teaching how to think is the most transformative act an educator can perform."

cards.title: From consumer to creator
cards.description: Every time a young person builds their first project, something shifts: they move from passive technology consumer to active creator of the digital world.

cards.title: Technology as amplifier
cards.description: Well-designed technology doesn't replace the teacher — it multiplies their impact. It's the difference between reaching 30 or 3,000 learners.

cards.title: Digital citizenship
cards.description: My goal isn't to train programmers — it's to build confident, critical and responsible digital citizens in the world we live in.

cards.title: Real impact
cards.description: When a senior sends their first video to their grandchild or a child programs their first robot — the impact is real, visible and transformative.

cv.subtitle: Learning Designer · Instructional Designer · EdTech & AI Educator · Programming & Robotics Teacher
about: I am a Learning Experience Designer and educator with over a decade of experience in education, technology, and digital innovation.
My work focuses on designing meaningful, hands-on learning experiences that combine technology, creativity, and real-world problem solving.

Currently, I work at CDI Portugal, where I design and coordinate educational programs in programming, robotics, artificial intelligence, and digital literacy, supporting children, youth, educators, and communities.

I am passionate about transforming complex technological concepts into engaging, accessible, and impactful learning experiences, especially through STEAM education, gamification, and project-based learning.
